purpose: Optional visual Solar System context. Not used by any terrain, visibility or metric calculation.
radiusNote: Mean of the three PCK radii (pck00011.tpc). Shown for apparent size only.

planets.name: Mercury
planets.positionNote: Barycentre of the Mercury system from DE440s. Mercury has no natural satellites, so the barycentre coincides with the planet centre.

planets.name: Venus
planets.positionNote: Barycentre of the Venus system from DE440s. Venus has no natural satellites, so the barycentre coincides with the planet centre.

planets.name: Mars
planets.positionNote: Barycentre of the Mars system from DE440s, used as a proxy for the planet centre (not the planet centre itself). The offset is negligible at this display's angular scale.

planets.name: Jupiter
planets.positionNote: Barycentre of the Jupiter system from DE440s, used as a proxy for the planet centre (not the planet centre itself). The offset is negligible at this display's angular scale.

planets.name: Saturn
planets.positionNote: Barycentre of the Saturn system from DE440s, used as a proxy for the planet centre (not the planet centre itself). The offset is negligible at this display's angular scale.

planets.name: Uranus
planets.positionNote: Barycentre of the Uranus system from DE440s, used as a proxy for the planet centre (not the planet centre itself). The offset is negligible at this display's angular scale.

planets.name: Neptune
planets.positionNote: Barycentre of the Neptune system from DE440s, used as a proxy for the planet centre (not the planet centre itself). The offset is negligible at this display's angular scale.

validation: Not compared with Horizons. Same SPICE call path as sky.json (spkpos, LT+S), which V1 checks only for the Sun and Earth seen from the sites.
limitations: System barycentres stand in for the centres of Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.
Visual context only. No visibility, occultation or brightness modelling for planets.
